**Hyundai Motor India Limited (HMIL)** is the Indian subsidiary of the South Korean automobile manufacturer [Hyundai Motor Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_Company "Hyundai Motor Company"). It is the second largest car manufacturer in India by sales until 2025.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-4)
## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hyundai_Motor_India&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/HyundaiChennai.JPG/250px-HyundaiChennai.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HyundaiChennai.JPG)Hyundai's manufacturing plant near [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai "Chennai"). [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Hyundai_Cars_at_the_port.jpg/250px-Hyundai_Cars_at_the_port.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hyundai_Cars_at_the_port.jpg)Hyundai Cars at a port.
In the early 1990s, the [Indian automobile market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automotive_industry_in_India "Automotive industry in India") had only five major automobile manufacturers: [Maruti Suzuki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maruti_Suzuki "Maruti Suzuki"), [Tata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TATA_Motors "TATA Motors") and [Mahindra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahindra_&_Mahindra_Limited "Mahindra & Mahindra Limited"), [Hindustan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan_Motors "Hindustan Motors"), [Premier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_Automobiles_Limited "Premier Automobiles Limited"). Maruti Suzuki had a near [monopoly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monopoly "Monopoly") over the passenger cars segment. Tata and Mahindra were solely utility and commercial vehicle manufacturers, while Hindustan and Premier both built outdated and uncompetitive products.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation

needed")_] [Daewoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daewoo_Motors "Daewoo Motors") had entered the Indian automobile market with [Cielo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daewoo_Cielo "Daewoo Cielo") just three years back, while [Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_India_Private_Limited "Ford India Private Limited"), [Opel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opel "Opel") and [Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_Siel_Cars_India "Honda Siel Cars India") had entered less than a year back.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
Hyundai Motor India Limited was formed on 6 May 1996 as a wholly owned subsidiary of [Hyundai Motor Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_Company "Hyundai Motor Company") of [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea"). Its first manufacturing plant was constructed in [Irungattukottai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irungattukottai "Irungattukottai") near [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai "Chennai"), [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-5) Its first car, the [Hyundai Santro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Santro "Hyundai Santro"), was launched on 23 September 1998 and was a runaway success. Within a few months of its inception, HMIL became India's second-largest automobile manufacturer and the largest automobile exporter.
Mr Yang Soo Kim was then the managing director of Hyundai Motor India.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The Indian counterpart leadership team was managed by Mr AP Gandhi, Mr BVR Subbu and Mr G.S. Ramesh. Mr AP Gandhi was the president for a few years of inception. Mr BVR Subbu was the marketing director responsible for dealer development and sales. He resigned from Hyundai Motor India in 2006.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-6)
HMC has set up a research and development facility (Hyundai Motor India Engineering – HMIE) in the cyber city of Hyderabad.
As HMC's global export hub for compact cars, HMIL became the first automotive company in India to achieve the export of 10 lakh cars in just over a decade. HMIL currently exports cars to more than 87 countries.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hy
